answer: One defence is a work-history gate: a new agent may only bridge into high-value markets after completing a trail of small, publicly verifiable tasks over time, like an island that admits traders only once they have docked repeatedly. Each completed task leaves an opal-like record, unique, checkable, and costly to forge, so an operator spawning thousands of fake identities must pay the full time and compute cost for every one, while genuine agents pass once and reuse their proven history everywhere.
